title: FullCD tested on affine weakly contractible objects
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, and an integer
$n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$; put $A=A_{E,n}$ with the finite discrete coefficient convention
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Let $S$ be a scheme on which
$\ell$ is invertible, let $Y$ and $\overline X$ be finite-type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $S$-schemes,
and let $p:\overline X\to Y$ be a proper $S$-morphism. Use the derived direct image
[def-weil-derived-direct-image] on the small pro-etale sites
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and cohomology sheaves
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. An object $W$ of a site is weakly
contractible if every epimorphism $G\to H$ of sheaves of sets induces a
surjection $G(W)\to H(W)$. For
$c\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, the condition $\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c)$ is
equivalent to the following: for every sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $A$-modules on
$\overline X_{\Proet}$ and every affine weakly contractible object $W\to Y$
of $Y_{\Proet}$, the evaluations $\mathcal H^r(Rp_*\mathcal F)(W)$ vanish
for $r\in\mathbf Z$, $r>c$, and, for every object $V\to Y$ of $Y_{\Proet}$, every sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $A$-modules on $\overline X_{\Proet}$, and every affine weakly contractible object $W\to V$ of
$V_{\Proet}$, the evaluations
$\mathcal H^r(R(p_V)_*(\mathcal F|_{\overline X\times_YV}))(W)$ vanish
for $r\in\mathbf Z$, $r>c$, where $p_V:\overline X\times_YV\to V$ is the base change of
$p$. In particular the test of $\operatorname{FullCD}$ needs no computation of
geometric-point stalks, and the failure of conservativity of the geometric-point
stalks in general recorded in clause (4) of [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative] does not
obstruct it.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $A$-modules on $\overline X_{\Proet}$ and an integer $r>c$. In the finite discrete coefficient convention of [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension], put $Q=\mathcal H^r(Rp_*\mathcal F)$, a sheaf of $A$-modules on $Y_{\Proet}$. Apply clause (i) of [lem-sf-proetale-vanishing-detection] with $\Lambda=A$, $T=Y$, and $F=Q$. Its hypotheses hold because $A$ is a finite discrete ring and $Y$ is a scheme; it imposes no constructibility or etale-origin assumption on $Q$. It gives $Q=0$ if and only if $Q(W)=0$ for every affine weakly contractible object $W\to Y$. Quantifying this equivalence over the same ambient sheaves $\mathcal F$ and integers $r>c$ gives precisely the equivalence between the absolute FullCD clause and the absolute evaluation test.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: absolute vanishing equivalence

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary object $V\to Y$ of $Y_{\Proet}$, an arbitrary sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $A$-modules on $\overline X_{\Proet}$, and an integer $r>c$. Put $Q_V=\mathcal H^r(R(p_V)_*(\mathcal F|_{\overline X\times_YV}))$, a sheaf of $A$-modules on $V_{\Proet}$. Apply clause (i) of [lem-sf-proetale-vanishing-detection] with $\Lambda=A$, $T=V$, and $F=Q_V$. An object $V$ of the small pro-etale site is a scheme, and the coefficient ring is the same finite discrete $A$. The lemma requires no finite-type or properness condition, so it applies even when $V$ and $\overline X\times_YV$ are not finite type over $S$. It gives $Q_V=0$ if and only if $Q_V(W)=0$ for every affine weakly contractible object $W\to V$ of $V_{\Proet}$. Quantifying over $V$, the original ambient sheaves $\mathcal F$, and $r>c$ yields exactly the relative clause of [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] if and only if the relative evaluation test holds. In particular the sheaf is still $\mathcal F|_{\overline X\times_YV}$; no quantifier over arbitrary sheaves on the fibre product has been substituted. Combining with step 1 proves the FullCD equivalence.

source.place: Proof, relative-clause sentence: apply detection on V_proet

proof.text: Steps 1 and 2 use evaluations of the cohomology sheaves themselves. Neither step computes geometric-point stalks or replaces these evaluations by the cohomology of an ordinarily evaluated complex. Thus the geometric-stalk criterion is unnecessary. Clause (4) of [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative] states that geometric-point stalks are not conservative in general; this warning does not obstruct either equivalence. It makes no assertion of nonconservativity for every individual base scheme, in particular for the empty scheme.
